content: The optimal treatment approach for adult T-cell leukemia (ATL) is determined by the specific clinical subtype of the disease. For patients with chronic or smoldering ATL, management often involves observation, skin-directed therapies, or a combination of zidovudine and interferon therapy. In contrast, patients with acute ATL are typically treated with chemotherapy, supportive care, allogeneic stem cell transplantation, or a combination of zidovudine and interferon therapy. For adult T-cell lymphoma, treatment generally includes chemotherapy, supportive care, or allogeneic stem cell transplantation. Management of Chronic/Smoldering Adult T-cell Leukemia Patients with chronic or smoldering ATL may be managed through observation and close follow-up to monitor for any symptomatic progression. Regular follow-up evaluations should include: A thorough history and physical examination. Assessment of blood urea nitrogen (BUN). Evaluation of serum creatinine levels. Imaging studies such as chest and abdominal CT scans. For patients with localized cutaneous lesions, skin-directed therapies may be employed. These include: Topical corticosteroids. Topical chemotherapy agents like mechlorethamine. Localized radiation therapy, with doses ranging from 8 to 36 Gy. Topical retinoids, such as bexarotene or tazarotene. Phototherapy, including UVB or narrowband UVB for patchy or thin plaques, and PUVA for thicker plaques. Topical imiquimod. For patients undergoing zidovudine and interferon combination therapy, the response to treatment should be evaluated after two months. If the patient responds to therapy, treatment with zidovudine and interferon should be continued. If there is no response, management should shift to either chemotherapy or supportive care, depending on the patient’s preferences. Complete remission in ATL is defined by the following criteria: No lymphadenopathy. No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly. Absence of cutaneous lesions. No malignant cells on peripheral blood smear. No malignant cells on bone marrow biopsy. Management of Acute Adult T-cell Leukemia First-line chemotherapy regimens for acute ATL include: CHOP: Cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone. CHOEP: Cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, etoposide, and prednisone. Dose-adjusted EPOCH: Etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, and doxorubicin. HyperCVAD: Cyclophosphamide, vincristine, doxorubicin, and dexamethasone, alternating with high-dose methotrexate and cytarabine. Patients who respond to first-line chemotherapy should be considered for allogeneic stem cell transplantation. For those who do not respond to initial therapy, second-line chemotherapeutic agents may be used, including: Bendamustine. Belinostat. Brentuximab vedotin (for systemic CD30+ peripheral T-cell lymphoma). DHAP: Dexamethasone, cisplatin, and cytarabine. ESHAP: Etoposide, methylprednisolone, cytarabine, and cisplatin. Dose-adjusted EPOCH. GDP: Gemcitabine, dexamethasone, and cisplatin. GemOx: Gemcitabine and oxaliplatin. ICE: Ifosfamide, carboplatin, and etoposide. Pralatrexate. Romidepsin. Patients who respond to second-line chemotherapy should also be considered for allogeneic stem cell transplantation. For chronic or smoldering ATL patients treated with zidovudine and interferon, response should be assessed after two months. Responders may either continue zidovudine and interferon therapy or proceed to allogeneic stem cell transplantation. Non-responders should be managed with either chemotherapy or supportive care, based on patient preferences. Management of Adult T-cell Lymphoma The initial management of adult T-cell lymphoma involves first-line chemotherapy regimens, which include: CHOP: Cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone. CHOEP: Cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, etoposide, and prednisone. Dose-adjusted EPOCH: Etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, and doxorubicin. HyperCVAD: Cyclophosphamide, vincristine, doxorubicin, and dexamethasone, alternating with high-dose methotrexate and cytarabine. Patients who respond to first-line chemotherapy should be considered for allogeneic stem cell transplantation. For those who do not respond, second-line chemotherapeutic agents may be used, including: Bendamustine. Belinostat. Brentuximab vedotin (for systemic CD30+ peripheral T-cell lymphoma). DHAP: Dexamethasone, cisplatin, and cytarabine. ESHAP: Etoposide, methylprednisolone, cytarabine, and cisplatin. Dose-adjusted EPOCH. GDP: Gemcitabine, dexamethasone, and cisplatin. GemOx: Gemcitabine and oxaliplatin. ICE: Ifosfamide, carboplatin, and etoposide. Pralatrexate. Romidepsin. Patients who respond to second-line chemotherapy should also be considered for allogeneic stem cell transplantation. Supportive Therapy Prophylaxis against opportunistic infections is essential for ATL patients. Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim is recommended to prevent such infections.
